title: SABA/4/2023 of VASEEM Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY, MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS, U.K. DEHRADUN

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Anticipatory Bail Application No.4 of 2023
Vaseem and another ........Applicants

Present:-
Mr. Dheeraj Joshi, Advocate for the applicants.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, Deputy Advocate General with Ms. Meena
Bisht, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicants Saseem and Arshalan are in judicial
custody in FIR/Criminal Case No.28 of 2023, dated
26.02.2023, under Sections 307, 333, 353, 34 IPC, Police
Station Cantt., District Dehradun. This is the second
anticipatory bail application of the applicant. Their first
anticipatory bail application was dismissed as withdrawn
on 28.03.2023.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the FIR, Constable Manoj Kumar
had telephonically contacted Constable Deepak Kumar
that he had intercepted a tractor which was carrying
mines and minerals. The tractor was being occupied by
the applicants and others. When police party reached at

2
the spot, they found Constable Manoj Kumar was in a
injured condition, lying in a pool of blood. Subsequently,
it was revealed that the applicants and the co-accused
were moving in a tractor after theft the mines and
minerals, when the Police Constable Manoj Kumar
intercepted them, they ran over their tractor over him,
due to which, he was seriously injured. He was admitted
in the hospital and the FIR was lodged by Sub-Inspector
Sandeep Devrani.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the involvement of Constable Manoj Kumar is
doubtful. He would refer to news paper reporting, which
is Annexure No.2 to this anticipatory bail application, to
argue that, in fact, SSP had ordered for inquiry.
5. State despite objections has not chosen to file
objections. The Court does not intend to comment on the
functioning of the State Government in filing objections
before this Court. The Court leaves it as it.
6. First and foremost, the news paper cuttings
may not be basis for the order of the Court; secondly, it
also speaks that there was an attack on a Police
Constable.

3
7. FIR is quite categorical what the applicants
have done. According to it, the applicants were in the
process of carrying stolen mines and minerals when they
were intercepted by the Police Constable; they attacked
the Police Constable, due to which, he was seriously
injured and admitted in the hospital.
8. Having considered the nature of offence and
other attending factors, this Court is of the view that
there is no ground to enlarge the applicants on
anticipatory bail. Accordingly, second anticipatory bail
application of the applicants deserves to be rejected.
9. The second anticipatory bail application is
rejected.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 13.06.2023
Sanjay
